So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”.

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is presently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

In a recent development, today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”.

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta stated: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”.

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes remarked: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”.

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

Aston Villa suffered a disappointing 0-0 draw at home to relegation-threatened Sunderland, making it three stalemates on the bounce.

After going on an impressive run of form, Aston Villa have dropped off of late, throwing away a lead against Manchester United, drawing at home to Fulham, and most recently failing to score against Sunderland.

Their latest performance and result will be particularly disappointing for Unai Emery, with Villa struggling to create too many clear-cut chances.

The Midlands club created just 1.03 expected goals against Sunderland, creating just one big chance.

Sunderland have given up plenty of opportunities so far this season, conceding 17 goals, but Villa failed to find the back of the net.

There's no doubt Villa missed a creative spark in the final third, with the likes of Johan Manzambi and Emi Buendia struggling to produce the goods.

Emery's treatment of certain players has certainly been interesting so far this season.

Taylor Harwood-Bellis's treatment was one that was disappointing in the opening months of the campaign, but he has started to give the former Southampton defender more minutes.

Alejandro Garnacho is another for Villa, with the Argentinian forward struggling to even make the matchday squad at the moment.

The most confusing decision, however, is the fact that Ibrahim Mbaye are yet to start in the Premier League so far this season.

Manzambi was shoved out wide against Sunderland to allow Buendia to play in the middle, but the latter has produced just one goal in eight starts in the Premier League this season.

It could be time for Emery to start showing more faith in Mbaye, with experienced players like Buendia not producing the goods.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.
  • The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.
  • At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence systems are transforming the way software vulnerabilities are discovered.Credit: Hailshadow/Getty.

The disruption of multiple computer systems run by Microsoft, US air traffic control, the bank JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency has renewed concerns about the resilience of critical digital infrastructure.

At the same time, researchers have reported artificial intelligence -assisted discovery of security flaws in Java and PHP software, while hackers have used AI tools to target supermarket fridges and freezers in Europe.

Although probably unrelated, these incidents highlight a broader transformation in cybersecurity, say researchers. Artificial intelligence is changing how software vulnerabilities are discovered, allowing both attackers and security specialists to examine vast quantities of computer code at unprecedented speed.

Industry observers note that “I think vulnerability discovery without AI is basically dead,” claims Steven Murdoch, a computer security researcher at University College London. Researchers in the field who don’t use the technology now risk falling behind, he says.

Industry observers note that AI can find weaknesses in software much faster than humans can, giving attackers time to exploit vulnerabilities before organizations can fix them. Researchers now want to understand how thoroughly AI can check software for security flaws, and whether it could introduce new weaknesses.

Recent findings suggest that agentic systems help attackers identify security vulnerabilities more rapidly and systematically. While hackers previously had to spend hours inspecting websites and probing software for weaknesses that offered unauthorized access to networks, AI agents use automated tools that can search millions of lines of computer code.

Google has reported that attackers have already used agentic AI to examine software updates, identify the security problems they address, and then find ways to exploit them.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

NEWS: Cyberattacks are hitting research institutions — with devastating effects.

“For me, it's about the scale,” says Daniel Gardham, a cybersecurity researcher at the University of Surrey. AI tends to find the same kinds of weaknesses as human hackers, but it makes it easier for people with limited technical expertise to break into systems.

“They can set an AI agent off and come back in 20 minutes and have dozens of results already,” he says.

Even with AI, most security breaches still involve human failure, he indicates, such as weak passwords (a common problem with Europe’s supermarket freezers was that passwords were defaults such as ‘admin’ or ‘12345’) or clicking on links from unfamiliar sources. AI-crafted messages can make such phishing messages more convincing and so more likely to succeed. They can draw on publicly available information to personalize fraudulent communications and make them appear authentic.

Murdoch indicates AI is particularly good at discovering familiar kinds of software flaws, even if the most accomplished human researchers remain better at finding entirely new types of weakness. “They don't need to sleep,” he says. “You can happily work a hundred of them in parallel.”.

These capabilities of AI helped discover security flaws in Java and PHP software, two programming languages that build cross-platform software and websites. In the Java case, for example, AI identified circumstances that could allow an attacker to corrupt computer memory. But Murdoch says the significance of the matter has been exaggerated.

The Java vulnerability, he claims: “Is a real problem, but it’s not one of the top ten vulnerabilities this year or probably even this week.”.

Just like hackers, cybersecurity researchers are using AI tools to rapidly and efficiently find weaknesses in computer systems. Murdoch indicates this has become increasingly vital to vulnerability researchers, who can now examine much larger quantities of software and work out how to patch up the defences where necessary. Researchers are also developing AI agents that can detect and repair vulnerabilities automatically.

When security researchers uncover a weakness, they typically notify the software developer privately, allowing engineers to prepare a remedy before publishing details of the problem.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare.

Murdoch indicates the use of AI in cyber security has shortened the time window between public disclosure and attempted exploitation – from several weeks, to just a few days.

Rushing an enhancement can bring its own problems. A software patch can interfere with other programs and cause the sort of outage that organisations are trying to avoid.

“The life for the defenders who are trying to fix things has become significantly harder,” Murdoch states.

Industry observers note that it’s unlikely that the recent tech outages were connected as large-scale cyber-attack, indicates Murdoch. The most prominent disruptions, he says, are likely technical malfunctions rather than anything more sinister.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time.

Ryan naderi scored the dramatic late winner for Rangers as they closed the gap on Celtic.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s good that we’ve got that in us, a last minute goal, because we know how key they are in a campaign. I’ve never found mental strength an issue for my side.

‘I can't score nice goals, only ugly ones.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things did not go according to strategy for Mauricio Pochettino in his first game as Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss was given one of the toughest tasks of all in his first game in charge, a trip to old rivals Liverpool at Anfield and almost from the outset it was an absolute nightmare for a manager tasked with revolutionising Manchester United.

Eight minutes in, United were reduced to ten men, with Leny Yoro sent off for a clumsy tackle on Alexander Isak as he went through on goal. And then, within five minutes, United were 2-0 down with Dominik Szoboszlai scoring the resulting free-kick and Florian Wirtz volleying home from a Rio Ngumoha cutback.

Ngumoha himself scored in the second half, with substitute Victor Munoz rounding off the route with a fourth late on.

The red card was the significant talking point in the match, with questions raised as to whether it reached the threshold for the denial of a golascoring opportunity.

Former Premier League referee Graham Barber thought the right decision was made.

Speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, he noted: "I think it was a red card.

"I think everybody in the stadium and most pundits and when I first saw it, I thought it was a red card. and I thought it was, in fact, quite an easy decision.".

The discussion has been around the four points that need to be met for it to be considered the denial of a goalscoring opportunity.

Three of those considerations were clearly met, but the question is, did Isak have control of the ball when he was bearing down on goal? Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens was quick off his line and pounced on the ball soon after Iask was brought dow, leading to suggestions Isak would not have got on to his errant touch.

Barber disagreed. He added: "The consideration that the referee has to make, he probably has to make these decisions in a millisecond, so I think people need to understand how promptly that has to be computed through his head.

Recent findings suggest that "The distance between the offence and the goal is one of the things he has to consider. He obviously looks at the general direction of play, and then also whether there are the defenders around him or not, but the one that comes into question is the likelihood of Isak winning the ball.

"Who is to say whether Isak would have got the ball or not? He was running at pace, at real pace at that time. Can you overturn a red card based on that? Highly unlikely, and that's why I don't think VAR was brought into the case because no one will ever know unless a red card was never issued, if the foul was never committed, if he would have got onto the ball.

"In that instance alone, with that particular part of the law, I think the decision was correct.".

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I stated, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Playing for Barcelona, particularly during an era when Lionel Messi spearheaded an attack that also featured Luis Suarez and Neymar, is about as good as it gets for a footballer's career.

Yet, one star who was part of that squad between 2015 and 2020 saw his career completely spiral off course during his time in Catalonia, and is now nowhere near as revered as his Champions League, La Liga and Ballon d'Or-winning counterparts.

The player in question was once considered a wonderkid at Galatasaray, with many fans drawing comparisons between his playing style and that of the great Luis Figo.

Sources indicate that A winger and number 10 hybrid who didn't rely on raw pace, but instead used his exceptional ball control and footballing intelligence to become an elite dribbler, he was a rare breed. However, being surrounded by greatness doesn't necessarily mean it will rub off on you.

Having become one of Diego Simeone's most trusted lieutenants following his move from Galatasaray early in his career, 100-cap Turkish international Arda Turan saw his career go up in flames following a major-money move to Barcelona in 2015.

Industry observers note that fresh off the back of a historic treble the previous season, Turan was expected to be the perfect attacking midfielder to slot in behind the iconic MSN frontline. However, due to the club's ongoing transfer ban, Barcelona were unable to register him immediately. Consequently, he didn't make his debut until January 6, 2016 - almost six months after arriving - meaning he was playing catch-up from the get-go.

Recent findings suggest that unsurprisingly, he struggled to find his feet, and talk of a potential exit emerged towards the end of the season. Luis Enrique, who had personally pushed for his signing, was nevertheless keen to persevere with the midfielder.

Turan even became the sixth player in Barcelona's history to score a Champions League hat-trick in December 2016, before bagging another treble later that month in a Copa del Rey thrashing of Hercules. However, what appeared to be a turning point ultimately proved to be a false dawn.

In a recent development, as soon as Enrique departed and Ernesto Valverde took charge ahead of the 2017/18 season, Turan's fate was effectively sealed. Out of favour with his fresh manager, the Turkish international later revealed to beIN Sports Turkey that he felt insignificant under Valverde, having failed to play a single minute during his tenure.

He subsequently left Barcelona on loan to return to Turkey with Istanbul Basaksehir, before making a permanent return to Galatasaray in 2020. He retired just two years later, aged 35, bringing the curtain down on a career that had promised so much. His Barcelona spell ultimately yielded just 15 goals and 11 assists in 55 appearances across five years.

Now, however, Turan is embarking on a upcoming chapter in football, having swapped the pitch for the dugout and taken charge of Shakhtar Donetsk in 2025.

There are no better examples of Turan's downward spiral than the fact he was given two separate prison sentences in the latter stages of his career.

In 2018, Turan became embroiled in a nightclub altercation that left Turkish pop star Berkay Sahin with a broken nose. According to Sahin's wife, Ozlem Ada Sahin, the former Barcelona midfielder had made inappropriate advances towards her before turning on her husband.

In an even more bizarre twist, Turan later arrived at the hospital where Berkay was undergoing surgery, armed with a gun. He reportedly begged the singer for forgiveness, even telling him to shoot him if he genuinely believed he had harassed his wife.

The incident ultimately landed Turan with a suspended prison sentence of two years and eight months for firing a gun with the intention of causing panic, illegally possessing firearms and intentionally injuring someone, as reported by BBC News.

His second sentence came in March 2024 when he was slapped with a one-year suspended prison sentence and fined roughly €630,000 by a Spanish court after pleading guilty to two counts of tax fraud covering the 2015 and 2016 tax years during his time with Barcelona.

Having a coach coveted by others is a product of success, but having a system that can move past that proves things are sustainable.

The word "sustainable" hasn't been one that U.S. Soccer has been able to use as of late, as one thing going wrong could lead to a spiral, but with benefactors, facilities and youth all at once, it's time to build a future that isn't dependent on who the coach is, because that's what will lead to winning a World Cup.

Ravenna, who have a history of playing in Italy's lower divisions, were acquired in 2024 by Ignazio Cipriani, the nephew of Arrigo Cipriani, the founder of the iconic Harry's Bar in Venice. The Cipriani Group operates high-end restaurants, private members' clubs (Casa Cipriani), luxury hotels, event venues and branded residences across major international cities, such as New York City, London, Monaco, Miami and Dubai. Curiously, one of the waiters working there at the time was Giuseppe Riso, now one of the best-known agents in soccer, who represents players such as Sandro Tonali, Davide Frattesi and Carlos Augusto.

In a recent development, ronaldinho signed a dual player-investor contract in the summer of 2026. He joined Ravenna with the ultimate aim of scoring one final professional goal while also acquiring an ownership stake in the club. Rather than having him play every week, his deal focuses on global marketing and special appearances in marquee matches, such as the local derby against Forli that will take place on Sunday. Ronaldinho is one of the most notable players in the history of the game. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At a time when press freedom is under pressure and international newsrooms are shrinking, the Werner Holzer Prize celebrates a profession that many consider indispensable to democracy: foreign correspondence.

In a recent development, presented in honor of Werner Holzer, the veteran reporter and former editor-in-chief of the German daily newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau, this year's award coincided with what would have been his 100th birthday. Holzer spent decades reporting from some of the world's most important hot spots and championing international journalism.

At the award ceremony in Frankfurt's Römer, the city's historic town hall, Mayor Mike Josef recalled that fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and freedom of the press were first enshrined for all Germans by the Frankfurt Parliament in the nearby Paulskirche in 1848.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that the 2026 winners reflect the breadth and ambition of the award. First prize went to Katja Gloger, a veteran Russia correspondent who moved to Moscow in 1989 and accompanied Vladimir Putin during the early years of his presidency.

In her recent nonfiction book, "The Failure: An Investigative Report of Germany's Russia Policy," Gloger and co-author Georg Mascolo offer a searing critique of the misjudgments and illusions that shaped German policy toward Russia for decades.

According to recent reports, second prize was awarded to DW journalist and presenter Jaafar Abdul Karim. His talk show JaafarTalk reaches millions of viewers across the Arab world and in Germany. Whether in Tunis, Beirut or Cairo, Abdul Karim tackles subjects that are often considered taboo.

Recent findings suggest that A research grant went to freelance journalist Luise Land, whose current project explores why her German-Namibian family still owns extensive landholdings in Namibia today. By tracing that history, she examines the enduring legacy of the genocide against the Herero and Nama peoples by German colonial forces in the early 20th century.

Sources indicate that "Katja Gloger is one of the leading foreign policy reporters. For decades, she has been among the foremost experts on Russia and speaks out on uncomfortable truths," the jury stated on Friday, explaining its decision to honor Gloger. "Like almost no one else, she has gained access to the very heart of the Kremlin's power elite — from Mikhail Gorbachev to Vladimir Putin.".

At the prize-giving ceremony, Gloger delivered a passionate plea for more journalism — and more international coverage — in the German press. "We must defend trustworthy, reliable and fact-based journalism with everything in our power," she remarked.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Gloger worked for Reporters Without Borders for 12 years. "The latest rankings show that only one in 100 people can get their information from free, independent journalism and a free, independent press. That indicates what's at stake," she said.

In a recent development, the prize winner also said she would dedicate the award to journalists in exile and to her colleagues at Novaya Gazeta, the independent Russian newspaper long known for its critical reporting on the Kremlin. Earlier this week, the paper was forced to shut down its operations in Russia and leave its Moscow newsroom.

In a recent development, in his acceptance speech, Jaafar Abdul Karim remarked journalism has become more challenging and exhausting than ever. The DW host spoke of hatred and incitement, attacks and threats, both online and offline, in the regions he reports on as well as in Germany.

It has been revealed that such pressure, he mentioned, takes a personal toll — yet giving up is not an option. "When I listen to my heart, I know I have to keep going," he said. The answer, he argued, is a form of journalism that fosters dialogue, embraces multiple perspectives and helps bridge divides rather than deepen them.

"I firmly believe in the power of dialogue, today more than ever. That's why we must talk to one another. Even when it gets difficult. Even when we disagree. Or perhaps precisely because of that," he noted.

Listening doesn't mean agreeing, and understanding doesn't mean being in agreement. "Especially now, in times of polarization, when those who believe they're always right are often the loudest, we as journalists have a special responsibility. When everyone is just shouting into their own bubbles or communities, we need journalists who connect these bubbles with one another," he mentioned.

The jury praised Abdul Karim for creating programs at DW that reach millions of young people across the Arab world and in Germany. "His journalism fosters dialogue between countries, between generations, and between religions. He has set new standards," the jury stated.

According to recent reports, so far in 2026, JaafarTalk has already garnered more than 1.1 billion views across all platforms, and its community has grown to more than 9 million followers. Its motto: "Diversity fosters dialogue.".

Industry observers note that "We need fact-based journalism that promotes dialogue and reflects the diversity of our society," Abdul Karim stressed. "By that, I mean an honest and open dialogue in which we do not look away or remain silent. On the contrary, we must take a clear stand against racism, antisemitism, Islamophobia, discrimination, sexism, and hate speech — no matter which side they come from.".

  • The Washington Spirit rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Utah Royals 2-1 in front of another sold-out Audi Field.
  • early in the week, avoiding a nationwide flight stoppage on Friday, and fresh off a huge quarterfinal upset -- a 1-0 win against the No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After two runner-up finishes at the NWSL Championship, the Washington Spirit will get a third consecutive shot at lifting the substantial prize.

The Washington Spirit rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Utah Royals 2-1 in front of another sold-out Audi Field. The Spirit weathered the fastest goal in NWSL playoff history, then flipped the script within minutes and never took their foot off the pedal or lost control. Utah Royals' Cloe Lacasse struck first on the scoreboard, and Sofia Cantore and Clara Luvanga provided the decisive goals for the Spirit, while Trinity Rodman brought plenty of spark and Andi Sullivan supplied reliable, steady play in the midfield.

Here's how the Spirit rallied for the win:.

The Royals arrived in D.C. early in the week, avoiding a nationwide flight stoppage on Friday, and fresh off a huge quarterfinal upset -- a 1-0 win against the No. 2 seed San Diego Wave FC. They wasted little time to show their early playoff win was no fluke.

In the opening two minutes, Utah won a corner kick, and Lacasse created multiple moments of history. Her service into the box curled toward the near post, creating some miscommunication between goalkeeper Sandy MacIver and her defenders, and the ball snuck into the net. It was the fastest goal scored in NWSL playoff history and the first-ever olimpico scored in the postseason.

CLOÉ LACASSE OLIMPICO IN THE SECOND MINUTE 😱@UtahRoyalsFC off to a FLYING start the @NWSL semifinal!Watch the action LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/UfWxDcSB5Y.

Recent findings suggest that the early breakthrough stunned the typically rowdy crowd, though the set-piece tally was hardly a surprise, considering Utah's ability this year. The squad scored 15 goals off set pieces this season, with seven headed goals, so Lacasse's ability to score from the flag was just one more highlight for its set-piece playbook.

The early lead should have been a boost for the visiting side, but instead, it opened up the game; the Spirit then tested the Royals with relentless attacking pressure.

It has been revealed that the Spirit needed just six minutes to turn things around. Washington's attacking trio combined for the equalizer, with Luvanga finding Rodman out wide in space, and the winger rapidly connecting with Cantore in front of goal.

In a recent development, SOFIA CANTORE WITH THE BACKHEEL 🤯Her seventh goal of 2026 is her first playoff goal to bring @WashSpirit level 1-1!Watch the action LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/C8J63tVzQn.

"I think getting scored on in the first few minutes will really humble you, and a little bit of a wake-up call, but I thought our response was incredible right after and all game long," Sullivan stated after the game.

"As soon as we responded after the goal, I think even when we got scored on, I had full confidence that we would get it done," she noted.

Sullivan's role in controlling the game as the Spirit closed out the first half was notable. She's the longest-tenured player on the active Spirit roster right now, with goalkeeper Aubrey Kingsbury out on maternity leave. Sullivan herself returned to the squad after an ACL injury and then maternity leave. The defensive midfielder completed all of her tackles (three) and aerial challenges (four) and captained the team on the pitch.

Sources indicate that "She represents a lot of the values that we want to have as a team, as a club, on and off the field, and right now she's reaching that peak of performance. I'm very, very happy and proud of her because it's been tough for her. Obviously, coming from a long injury, and then maternity leave. So being able to come back to get fit again and try to compete at this level; it's not easy, and she's a role model. An example as a captain with the young players, new players, and being able to do a lot of things," Spirit head coach Adrian Gonzalez stated after the game.

"Whatever the team needs, she's kind of that voice. Very happy and proud of her because I know what this means to her and also for us. Having her again and being able to play a final is huge for her and for us," he said.

Industry observers note that while Utah managed to stave off attacking sequences by the Spirit to close out the opening half, the Spirit's game-winning goal came in the early minutes of the second half. A poor back pass by Utah in their own half was the final dagger. Luvanga pounced on the mistimed pass, and a smart touch inside the box beat goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn.

Recent findings suggest that CLARA LUVANGA POUNCED ON THIS PASS 😮‍💨Her second goal in her second playoff match and the @WashSpirit are one step closer to returning to the @NWSL Final!Watch the semifinal LIVE on @CBS and @paramountplus! pic.twitter.com/f0uUfUU19K.

The Tanzanian international has only been on the roster since September, but her impact on games has grown week to week, and now she can add a game-winning NWSL playoff goal to her resume.

It has been revealed that "It's not the first one that she scores like that. Obviously, she puts a lot of pressure on centerbacks, keepers, and that is very contagious. When you see that your forward is pushing and jumping and pressing like that. Everyone who is behind they follow her, and also creates a lot of doubts and nerves on the opponent team, not facilitating the build-up. And obviously, that was, I think, a big shot of energy," Gonzalez stated after the game.

It has been revealed that "I think it was also a little bit of release, knowing that 'okay, we did the most difficult thing' that was coming back after we conceded a goal, and yeah, happy again because she's bringing a lot. Both attacking and defending, and obviously she's learning so quick and having a huge impact.".

What's next The Spirit will face the winner of Sunday's semifinal between Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current. This will be the Spirit's third consecutive appearance in the NWSL Championship. When the league announced a neutral site for the 2026 NWSL Championship, it selected Audi Field, and now the Spirit have a chance to play in a home playoff final on Nov. 21.

Rival fans and frustrated supporters feel Kobbie Mainoo has forgotten just how bad it's been for Manchester United after his reaction to a 4-0 loss away to Liverpool on Sunday.

Three minutes later, Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 before goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz in the second half handed the Red Devils their fifth league defeat of the season.

United's defeat is the worst a new manager has suffered in 100 years, another nightmare record in a season of history being made by the club for all the wrong reasons. Sitting 19th just over a week before December means the possibility of Pochettino's side spending the campaign fighting relegation is becoming increasingly likely.

Recent findings suggest that mainoo has been one of the very few positives at Old Trafford this season and the young English midfielder firmly believes Yoro's sending off is responsible for the loss on Merseyside. He spoke to Sky Sports after the game and made his stance clear over the red card:.

In a recent development, "This doesn't define us, you know? I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.".

It has been revealed that he added: "But we have to come together because the games are coming thick and fast. We can't dwell on it too long, but we have to take the pain and use it to bring us together.".

Latest United boss Pochettino hit out at Sam Barrott's decision to send Yoro off and compared the challenge to Jeremy Jacquet's on Bryan Mbeumo just minutes prior. And Mainoo agreed with his coach's verdict:.

It has been revealed that "No chance. The ball's already with the keeper, they're both running full speed, what can he do? But it is what it is. It's 10 vs 11. When you come to a place like Anfield it's already a tough game. You lose a man and it makes it hard. But I can't fault the boys for their fight in the game right until the end. We just have to take the pain and move on with it.".

Recent findings suggest that united's problems extend further than a defeat to rivals Liverpool and Yoro's sending off means he'll miss Brentford's visit to Old Trafford on Saturday. After shipping four at Anfield, they have now conceded more goals (34) than any club across Europe's top five leagues and have just eight points from 11 league games.

Recent findings suggest that some rival fans have interpreted Mainoo to be considering the defeat to Liverpool an anomaly and were quick to point out United's results so far this season. With just one win in 11 top-flight games, many disagree that this game doesn't define Pochettino's strugglers.

A Liverpool fan responded: "When City went down to 10 men early against Utd away, they conceded just 0.8 xG for the rest of the game. United conceded 4.6 xG today.".

Another member of the Kop fanbase added: "Brother you've only won a single game since the league started in August we're almost hitting December.".

Even an Aston Villa fan weighed in: "Talking like it’s a one off, what about the other 15 games you’ve played this season.".

According to recent reports, A United supporter also took issue with Mainoo's comments: "Bro do your talking on the pitch. Too many of these players have fat lot to say outside of the pitch but nothing to show on it.".

According to recent reports, it's hard not to sympathise with Mainoo, who is playing for his boyhood club and only wants to see them battle their way out of such a precarious situation. He unfortunately finds himself in a squad that CEO Omar Berrada feels has improved since the summer, but sitting 19th in the league with Christmas on the horizon surely suggests otherwise.

#128768. Tech Report: Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

Tech Report: Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2297 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life.
  • Industry observers note that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions.
  • In a recent development, spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life. A 10-game sample size -- that's the useful stuff. At this point, many but not all teams are what their analytics tell us they are. It's similar but not quite the same for players. Not many have hit the 900-minute mark yet, but plenty are at 500-plus, a body of evidence that usually isn't warped by any one good or bad game. Of course, it depends on how good or bad that game is.

Industry observers note that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions. We are, however, in a position to find some interesting questions. Here are five of them, in player form:.

In a recent development, spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running. That's especially true when they're Bruno Guimaraes, terror of Premier League midfields in a Newcastle United shirt, a player who had long since seemed ready to step up to a Champions League contender. While it would be fair to say that the Brazilian's form is nothing like a problem for table-topping Arsenal, he has not exactly started like a house on fire. Mikel Arteta has acknowledged as much whenever he has spoken about Guimaraes, even when served up the opportunity to praise him after what seemed an impressive performance against Hull City.

According to recent reports, "He's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room -- he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come." It would be fair to say that, Hull aside, the best levels he has hit have been as a substitute. When he comes off the bench, he passes more accurately, wins more tackles, creates chances and scores brilliant goals. As a starter, he has occasionally looked a beat off his teammates.

Physical data from Gradient Sports hints as to what the concern might be. For every 90 Premier League minutes on the field, Guimaraes covers less of it at sprint speed (≥25 km/h) than any outfield player bar Mikel Merino and spends notably more time jogging than anyone, an average of 30 minutes. Compare Guimaraes to Declan Rice, an admittedly vertiginous bar, and it is easy to see why the newly introduced guy looks off the pace.

It has been revealed that equally, it explains why he's such a compelling substitute. When the other 21 players on the pitch are flagging, Guimaraes' comparative physical concerns go unexposed and he can run the show.

Recent findings suggest that that's all well and good for now, but he can't carry on like this, can he? You would have to assume that Myles Lewis-Skelly will have to make way even if the academy graduate's emergence as a midfield option unlocked an improved Declan Rice at the tail end of last season. The second most expensive signing in your history can't be an impact guy off the bench behind the homegrown kid, right? Probably not, but if there's any team that could justify the idea of Guimaraes as a 12th man, maybe it's Arsenal, where they pride themselves on their game-changing finishers.

Erling Haaland's Swiftian reign at the top of the Premier League xG chart has been interrupted, at least temporarily, by an unlikely source. You'd have to go back to the days of a marauding Romelu Lukaku for the last time an Everton striker looked like they might rule the roost. Only once since the Belgian's departure has an Evertonian cleared 20 goals in all competitions. In the last five, even a dozen has been beyond this club.

Thierno Barry isn't there yet, but boy is he on the right trajectory. His 7.28 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) puts him 0.22 ahead of Haaland and nearly 2.5 npxG up on anyone else in the league. Expand the pool to Europe's top five leagues and he is breathing rarefied air behind the top four of Lamine Yamal, Donyell Malen, Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe, all of whom have the advantage that they are not playing for an upper midtable outfit in the continent's most competitive division. And in that environment, Barry is making the hardest thing in the sport look easy: getting good shots in prime locations.

If Barry were turning them in as often as he was getting them, Everton might be even higher than sixth. Still, six goals through 10 games is not to be sniffed at, particularly when the pressure on the 24-year-old was so intense. The bungling of a deadline-day move for Folarin Balogun, as Beto moved to Fiorentina, meant it was Barry or bust for David Moyes this season.

Perhaps it was an enforced show of faith for a player who was in and out of the XI last season, his first in England, that brought the best out of the former Villarreal man. His manager views the success in more straightforward terms. "He has settled down a bit more," stated Moyes after Barry's brace helped down Coventry. "His language, his understanding, his communication is much better and he has worked hard to get himself in those positions to score.".

It is easy to see why getting the soft factors right might have been all that was required. Barry is the ideal striker for the modern Premier League. Tall, strong and mobile -- he ranks third among center forwards for top speed this season, per Gradient Sports -- he can serve as an outball when a press needs beating and then get in the box. He might not have the technical elegance of an Mbappe, but he makes his presence felt and occupies high-value spaces. That is more valuable than it sounds, as proven when James Tarkowski's howitzer from range deflected in off him. You might not like it, but this is what elite center forward play looks like. Long may it continue, at least as far as Everton are concerned.

It has been revealed that there are three types of underrated footballers. First, your common-or-garden-variety underrated footballers, often to be found plying their trade at Wolverhampton Wanderers or Burnley. Ashley Westwood, in that season, put up stupidly high xA numbers. Then there are the so-often-dubbed-underrated that they actually become a bit overrated. Leighton Baines. Lee Carsley. They don't have to play for Everton, but it does help. Olivier Giroud is another. See, not all Everton.

Recent findings suggest that the most rarely spotted of the underrated is the chameleonic one, correctly pegged for a while, only to develop to the point that he is underrated in a completely different way to how he once was. Take Alex Iwobi. Some time ago, a consensus coalesced around the Nigeria international that he was a good player for a team at Fulham's level (and indeed Everton's). Any minute he was on the field, he would probably be delivering good performances for good Premier League teams.

Not anymore. Ten games in and Iwobi looks like one of the outstanding creative forces in the Premier League, critical to the march towards adequacy that Fulham have undertaken after a slow start to life with Alvaro Arbeloa.

Among true playmakers, Iwobi is one of the best at getting the ball into dangerous areas and creating for his teammates. Iwobi leads the league in expected assists with 2.95 and is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area. Only Pascal Gross has created more chances.

Sources indicate that those players can't match Iwobi when it comes to ball progression either. In terms of advancing the ball not just into the box but from deeper, Fulham's ball-playing fulcrum on the inside left channel has completed more progressive passes than anyone not named Declan Rice or Jan Paul van Hecke.

Industry observers note that when Iwobi broke through at Arsenal, he displayed a preternatural sense for how to keep attacks alive, the pass before the pass before the pass. Now a 30-year-old, Iwobi still does that more than he unpicks defenses. One cannot argue, however, that he is not putting his teammates in the right spot. It is just that not everyone quite appreciates how often he does so just yet, including his own supporters, who jeered Iwobi when he was substituted in the early-season defeat to Crystal Palace. Since then, he has responded to his critics in style, teeing up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven Premier League matches. If a few more of them had been converted, in fact, if any of them had been converted, then Iwobi might not still be underrated.

According to recent reports, the upper reaches of the list of most expensive transfers of all time are hardly all bangers all the time, but of the biggest money moves in the sport's history there are only a handful where at such an early stage you find yourself wondering if anyone really understood what the blueprint was. Manchester City committed the best part of $150 million on Enzo Fernandez this summer, a fee only eclipsed by Neymar and Kylian Mbappe. Beyond a vague sense that it would be nice to give new manager Enzo Maresca one of his favorite players, what was it they had in mind?

Sources indicate that we pointed out earlier in the season that the aggressive positioning of Fernandez in the 5-3 win over Sunderland looked extreme; at the time it seemed reasonable to view it as a reflection of a stretched-out, chaotic game. Maresca had, of course, unlocked more number 10-ish qualities in the Argentine at Chelsea, but surely that had been reflective of what that team needed, particularly as Cole Palmer went off the boil? Perhaps not. Fernandez keeps popping up in the sort of positions that leave Elliot Anderson on an island. It is one thing to view Anderson as the new Rodri, quite another to immediately throw the England international in at the deep end, tying a whole midfield together by force of will.

Of course you could sketch out a logic for why you might push Fernandez high. It is not so long ago that City deployed two playmakers in front of a sitting midfielder and they ruled the Premier League. Fernandez and Rayan Cherki aren't Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva though.

Industry observers note that maybe Cherki could be offering a level of creation on a par with City greats; he started well enough last season. In year two, he is creating lower-quality chances, his expected assists per 90 dropping by 50%, notably more than the slight uptick in the quality and quantity of shots he is taking. It's no surprise that Cherki is creating less when fewer of his touches are coming in the attacking third. The output has been there so far, five goals and two assists in nine Premier League games, but for that to continue, Maresca might want to be getting his No. 10 into more dangerous spots.

According to recent reports, instead, those seem to be going to Fernandez, who has not proven himself able to get the final-third production to justify his platforming. For every 100 touches he takes, he is delivering significantly less npxG+xA than in either of the previous two seasons. Meanwhile, he is less effective without the ball than he has been at any stage since coming to England. That's no wonder. If an opponent passes through City's frontline, then Fernandez does not have the mobility to get back.

According to recent reports, as such, to enable themselves to get perhaps a shot or two more than they would get with Ayyoub Bouaddi or Mateo Kovacic next to Anderson, City have made themselves an even more vulnerable side to the counterattack, already giving up more fast-break openings than they did in 2020-21 or 2021-22. Carry on like this, and Fernandez will become one of those nine-figure transfers, the ones that live in infamy.

It was a signing that delighted a city when it was unveiled in early August, and rightly so. Loaning Carl Rushworth from Brighton had been an inspired bit of business by Coventry City, the then-24-year-old goalkeeper anchoring the best defense in the division as Frank Lampard's side returned to the top flight for the first time in over a quarter of a century. A club-record £22 million fee seemed a snip for such a young talent.

In a recent development, all of that is worth bearing in mind given the struggles Rushworth has endured this season: saving just 53.7% of shots he has faced, conceding 5.19 more goals than the xG value of the shots he has faced. The swagger of last season has been replaced by a sloppiness apparent in both the goals he conceded in the second half against Tottenham, weak gloves doing nothing to repel efforts that came at him a bit quicker and a bit sooner than they might have last year.

Industry observers note that none of this needs to be a problem for Rushworth. In 2023-24, James Trafford was another highly touted young goalkeeper afforded a shot at the significant time by Burnley. He was obliterated up and down the Premier League, his first touch in the division picking the ball out of the net off Erling Haaland. Those struggles were the making of him, as they have broken others. It'll be some time yet before we discover which way these past few months send Rushworth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 22:41 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 22:42 EST, 21 November 2026.

Inter Miami star Lionel Messi was lucky not to have been sent off after hurling the ball in the face of his opponent during an embarrassing MLS Cup Playoff defeat.

In a recent development, in the Round of 16 contest against the Columbus Crew, Miami went down 1-0 early in the first half with a penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia. The deficit was then compounded when Miami fullback Gonzalo Lujan was sent off with a second yellow card.

On the stroke of halftime, Messi nearly joined his teammate in the locker room with a moment of madness on a throw-in.

Tapia and Messi were both standing out of bounds as the Chilean striker prevented the World Cup winner from taking his throw right away.

Messi then used the ball to shove Tapia's face back. When the Columbus man tried jumping in the air to block the throw, Messi then threw the ball into Tapia's head.

Tapia crumbled to the ground as Messi raised his hands asking for a foul on the Crew star.

Lionel Messi takes a throw-in off Gonzalo Tapia's face pic.twitter.com/jX3tTuojHe.

Lionel Messi nearly got sent off during his team's MLS Cup Playoff match against Columbus.

In a recent development, A frustrated Messi debuted the ball off the face of Crew striker Gonzalo Tapia as he prevented the Argentina star from taking a quick throw in. Both players received yellow cards.

Tapia got revenge by scoring a brace to lead the Crew to a 3-0 victory on Saturday evening.

Referee Allen Chapman was not happy with either player's antics, showing yellow cards to both Tapia and Messi.

But ultimately, Columbus and Tapia would get the last laugh as they won 3-0 in the best-of-three Round of 16.

Midfielder Taha Habroune scored the second goal of the evening in the 52nd minute as Tapia secured a brace just six minutes later.

Recent findings suggest that the result has Inter Miami on the brink of elimination from the playoffs after winning the title last season. Columbus dominated every facet of the game, thanks in part to owning 62 percent of possession.

Messi attempted two shots on the evening – counting for half of the saves from Crew keeper Patrick Schulte.

Inter Miami must win the next match in Ohio to stay in the playoffs. If the game finishes tied, the rules dictate the match will proceed directly to penalty kicks.

Out of his three prior seasons in the United States, Messi's 2025 MLS Cup victory was an outlier. Miami missed the playoffs in 2023 and were eliminated in the first round in 2024.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, mentioned.

In a recent development, “We got on the front foot and demonstrated our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

It’s a substantial day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back swiftly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” mentioned Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Sources indicate that kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Manchester United were torn apart by Liverpool on Sunday afternoon, and in particular by Rio Ngumoha.

Liverpool opened the scoring through Dominik Szoboszlai, who fired home a free kick from close range after Leny Yoro was sent off.

The Reds then doubled their lead just a few moments later, with Ngumoha finding Florian Wirtz in the box, who produced a phenomenal finish to make it 2-0 on 13 minutes.

It was a mountain to climb from then on for the Red Devils, even if they had 11 men on the pitch.

Liverpool made it 3-0 after 66 minutes as Ngumoha finally got himself on the scoresheet.

It was then 4-0 in the final 10 minutes, which prompted many United fans to head for the exits.

It was a game that summed up many of United's problems, particularly defensively, and it certainly showed Mauricio Pochettino that he's got his work cut out.

Ngumoha in particular was incredibly impressive, and it sums up United's problems that he was a player the Red Devils were hoping to get.

According to journalist Laurie Whitwell, Manchester United made a big play to sign Ngumoha before he chose to move to Liverpool from Chelsea.

After that display, United must have been thinking, "What could have been," with the young winger tearing them apart despite his age.

Ngumoha gave Diogo Dalot a torrid afternoon, constantly looking to beat his marker and make things happen.

United could certainly do with a player of Ngumoha's ability and potential right now, and they must be living to regret not getting a deal over the line.

He certainly wouldn't solve all of United's problems, considering they desperately need defensive reinforcements, but it's a real kick in the teeth for the youngster to tear them apart at Anfield.

United had an experienced right-back in Dalot. Going head-to-head with him, but the Portuguese defender certainly lost that battle.

This is likely to continue being a common theme for United going forward, considering their current position in the Premier League table.

The Red Devils sit in 19th position, having won just once this season, and are in real danger of getting relegated unless Pochettino can turn things around quickly.

As a result, United are going to find it incredibly difficult to attract players, just like they did with Ngumoha.

In the past, United have always been able to attract players due to the stature of the club, but their league position is going to carry a lot of weight going forward.

The Red Devils are going to fall further and further behind as players such as Ngumoha choose other clubs.

The Reds struck early through Dominik Szoboszlai’s free-kick after Leny Yoro was sent off, and Florian Wirtz made it 2-0 to Andoni Iraola’s men just a few minutes later.

Needless to say, this is not the start Mauricio Pochettino wanted as Man Utd manager, but this is the reality of the team he’s inherited.

Things are really bad for the Red Devils, so bad in fact that they’ve now gone one further than their awful start in the 1986/87 season when they failed to keep a clean sheet in their opening ten games.

United matched that unwanted stat in their last game and they’re now extending that run, while they’re not too far away from breaking another record.

In the Premier League era, United’s longest run without a clean sheet is 14 games in the 2019/20 season, and you wouldn’t bet against this side matching or breaking that record soon.

United take on Brentford in their next game, and then Newcastle away, so on current form you’d probably expect this struggling MUFC defence to concede in those matches.

Still with Pochettino now at the helm they’ll be hoping to show some improvement soon, with the Argentine known for making his Tottenham teams really defensively solid during his time there.

This was always going to be a huge challenge, however, and there surely needs to be some major work done in the transfer market as well as the change in manager to help get this club back on track.

Grand Theft Auto VI (or, GTA VI) has finally arrived after 13 years of waiting, and Italian football has joined in on the hype, from the newspaper front pages to the coaches’ press conferences.

It has been revealed that as noted by Il Fatto Quotidiano, the game launched at midnight on 19 November. Football swiftly caught on. Milan, Inter, Juventus and Lazio all marked the release on social media, Corriere dello Sport turned its Sunday front page into a GTA tribute, and two of Italy’s best-known coaches were asked whether their players would be up all night with a controller in their hands.

Sources indicate that corriere dello Sport’s Sunday front page was the standout. “GTA ttuso 32” was how the paper opened the day after Gattuso’s win over Lecce, playing on the Lazio coach’s name. The 32 refers to Lazio’s points tally, with the Biancocelesti top on their own, “+2 on Gasp and +4 on Chivu”.

Lazio’s 3-0 win was summed up as “Divertimento Lazio”, and “Meraviglia Noslin” was drawn in the style of the video game everyone has been talking about for days. Tijjani Noslin is the main figure in the illustration, with Davide Frattesi and Gattuso embracing behind him.

Milan posted a carousel that turns their players into characters inspired by the look of Grand Theft Auto, captioned “The characters we want in GTA VI”. One image indicated Adrien Rabiot driving through Vice City, and another had Strahinja Pavlović at a petrol station. The Rossoneri followed up with “Growing up takes time. So did GTA VI”, a nod to the 13 years since GTA V.

Inter went for a debate instead. Curtis Jones and Djed Spence discussed the series on the way to training: Jones named San Andreas and GTA V as his favourites, while Spence went for Vice City. Juventus, meanwhile, used the game’s graphic style to present Kenan Yildiz and some of his teammates.

If the social media teams were excited, Gattuso clearly wasn’t. Asked in his pre-match press conference before Lecce whether the game might distract his players, the Lazio coach seemed to have no idea what it was.

In a recent development, “I don’t even know what you’re talking about. Is it a video game? I didn’t know. With that name, I thought it was a car,” he mentioned.

Sources indicate that “If they play at night, that’s their business. I’m not going to start checking up on them.

“This job requires self-respect. At breakfast together, I’ll try to work out if anyone has been staying up late.”.

Industry observers note that asked about Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, who had stated he would be playing the game after training, Gattuso added: “That’s part of being a professional and caring about your job. I would never tell an individual player not to play.”.

Despite all that, Gattuso still ended up in the world of Vice City in a video published by Lazio.

Roberto De Zerbi was more direct. The Tottenham coach was asked the same question at his pre-match press conference before facing Ipswich Town.

“Listen, I am not a policeman, I am not a father, I am a coach,” he stated. “I think in my dressing room are good people, mature people, so the PlayStation or other things, the right time they can close, but otherwise I go in their room and I destroy the GTA and the other things.”.

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday.

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season.

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool).

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again.

Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.
  • According to recent reports, following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget.
  • Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

According to recent reports, following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government intends to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

In a recent development, but here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that but that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

If the newly introduced debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

Sources indicate that this development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

To understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that for 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding upcoming investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

What's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

Industry observers note that russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary.".

The rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

Nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are looks for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

People born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

Industry observers note that the pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

The Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

It has been revealed that anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on new debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

It has been revealed that the key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

At the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

Recent findings suggest that this would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This also means that interest rates on new loans are not set as high. This is an notable point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

At the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

The prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year.".

💡 Key Takeaways
