  • This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.
  • Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that so much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

It has been revealed that jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had stated he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

Industry observers note that in between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

Spurs have taken the lead after Mateus Fernandes' corner ends up in Chelsea's goal ⚽️ https://t.co/X65gyO9yPX.

A man and a goal down, Chelsea then saw hundreds of their own fans walk out when Mathys Tel scored a brilliant second for Spurs with three minutes remaining. The visiting fans, who had seen one win at the Bridge since 1990 prior to Saturday, could hardly believe what they had seen.

"Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ.

Tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz.

Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

Recent findings suggest that tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

The missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

Recent findings suggest that kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

Industry observers note that it was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virgil van Dijk and David Raya are now two of the best players in the Premier League, accumulating 528 English top-flight appearances between them. Naturally, this means that the pair have played alongside some of the very best in the game.

Recent findings suggest that van Dijk made a name for himself in British football at Celtic and Southampton, before completing his massive move to Liverpool. At Anfield, he's established himself as one of the greatest defenders in Premier League history, whilst winning two league titles and a Champions League in the process.

Meanwhile, Raya doesn't quite have the longevity at the top level as his Dutch counterpart, but he has developed into one of the world's best goalkeepers since signing for Arsenal in 2023. Last year's Premier League title triumph strengthened his case for being the very best shot-stopper on the planet.

While the pair have had the pleasure of sharing dressing rooms with an array of world-class players, they've also played alongside several players who didn't quite reach the outstanding level that they did. Former Celtic number nine Anthony Stokes falls into that category.

Eight years after leaving Celtic, Stokes was sentenced to 15 months in prison.

It has been revealed that born in Dublin, Stokes joined Arsenal's academy at the age of 15. After developing through the Gunners' youth system, Stokes left the North London club after making just a single appearance for the first team.

In a recent development, he'd go on to have stints at Sunderland and Hibernian, before making his way to Celtic, where he enjoyed the most fruitful spell of his career. Netting 76 goals in 191 appearances for the Scottish giants, he then left Glasgow and spent the last six years of his career jumping from club to club, spending time in Greece, Azerbaijan, Turkey and Iran.

According to recent reports, three years after hanging up his boots, Stokes was arrested and found guilty of drug and driving offences. However, he successfully won an appeal against the verdict, and the sentence was eventually overturned.

Industry observers note that A prolific striker in his youth career at Arsenal, Arsene Wenger started to take note of Stokes heading into the 2005/06 season. In October 2005, the Frenchman called the then 17-year-old up to the Gunners' matchday squad for a League Cup tie against Sunderland.

Wenger handed Stokes his senior debut that day, introducing the Irishman in the 88th minute in place of Arturo Lupoli, with the North Londoners running out 3-0 winners. While this proved to be his one and only appearance for the Premier League giants' first team, it wasn't yet the end of him at Arsenal.

To aid his development by playing regular minutes, Wenger sent Stokes out to Falkirk on loan in 2006. The forward enjoyed a prolific stint at the Scottish club, scoring 16 goals in 18 appearances, prompting praise from the legendary Gunners coach upon his return to North London.

"Anthony has made a significant step up to the SPL and has done very well - I'm very happy about it. Ideally, I'd like all of our young kids on loan to come back to Arsenal." - Wenger on Stokes in 2006 (via BBC Sport).

Despite Wenger's words, there was no room for Stokes at Arsenal. He joined Sunderland in January 2007 for £2 million, and after struggling to make an impact at the Stadium of Light, he eventually made his way back to Scotland in 2009, signing for Hibernian.

Recent findings suggest that lighting up the Scottish Premiership again, scoring 23 goals in his solitary season at Hibs, Celtic came in and acquired the striker in August 2010. Signing a four-year contract in Glasgow, Stokes promptly established himself as a fan favourite at Celtic Park.

He enjoyed two seasons where he surpassed the 20-goal mark, and ultimately left the Bhoys with four Premiership winners' medals in his back pocket. This spell with the Hoops is where he met Van Dijk, whom he shared a dressing room with between 2013 and 2015, before the centre-back signed for Southampton.

After a loan spell back in Edinburgh with Hibs, Stokes briefly returned to English football, leaving Celtic for Blackburn Rovers in 2016. His stint in Lancashire wasn't very successful, making just 14 appearances for the Blues and Whites, although he did cross paths with future Yashin Trophy nominee Raya at Ewood Park.

Industry observers note that stokes then spiralled into a classic 'journeyman' path as he entered the latter stages of his career. He returned to Hibs for a third time, before playing for Apollon Smyrnis, Tractor, Adana Demirspor, Persepolis and Livingston, all in the space of four years.

Many thought his spell at Livingston would be his final, but Stokes returned to the game in August 2025, five years after last playing, signing for Conor McGregor's pub team, Black Forge.

Stokes had a history of criminal convictions before he was finally sentenced to prison in 2024. In 2013, the striker was convicted of assault after headbutting park attendant Anthony Bradley in a Dublin nightclub.

In 2019, he pleaded guilty to stalking his ex-girlfriend and her mother in Scotland. He spent short periods in prison for each of these offences before he was handed a 15-month sentence in 2024.

It has been revealed that the former professional footballer was caught following a high-speed car chase in Dublin and was reportedly found guilty of possessing £3,300 worth of cocaine in the process. Stokes was deemed to be over the alcohol limit and driving at 99mph when he nearly collided with another motorist in early January 2023.

He also entered an additional guilty plea to possessing 86 illegal street tablets in Dublin, ten days after the traffic pursuit.

Alongside his 15-month sentence, Stokes was banned from driving for five years. However, he was released within hours in order to appeal the severity of the sentence. In November 2024, his sentence was overturned on appeal, meaning he successfully evaded jail time.

We kept our heads in the game and started controlling it and in the second half we took the game by the scruff of the neck and highlighted the mentality. We didn’t slack off.

Sources indicate that “As fans they always want us to score chances and we know we should have scored more. Creating those chances is crucial as well. It’s about keeping a cool head and keeping composed and they will come.”.

Breaking: Kansas City Current's grit earns them spot in NWSL Championship while Gotham's logistics problems linger

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2245 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • FRESH YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches.
  • "I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".
  • Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FRESH YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune said post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

Icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game plan that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during New York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

Industry observers note that "We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins said. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

It has been revealed that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness concerns over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill noted. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In a recent development, in other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

In a recent development, gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of New York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Industry observers note that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

"As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match initiative that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

According to recent reports, the Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a plan," Armas remarked. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while at the moment headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

"Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros said. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up strategy for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull New York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

Sources indicate that "I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce said. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

Industry observers note that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

According to recent reports, "I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

"Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.
  • Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

In a recent development, an extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification currently. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

Industry observers note that we could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Industry observers note that cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

In a recent development, we wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

In a recent development, leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole revealed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that we are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

According to recent reports, colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

Recent findings suggest that for clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

It has been revealed that the tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him.

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Industry observers note that then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

According to recent reports, but the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are presently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal.

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

Sportswear giants adidas have linked up with Manchester-born streetwear brand Drama Call to deliver a nostalgic Manchester United collection inspired by the clubâs 1991 Cup Winnersâ Cup triumph.

The centrepiece of the drop is a reimagined version of the â91 final shirt â a design forever etched into United history.

Industry observers note that this updated take arrives in a long-sleeved white base with red Three Stripes, the adidas Trefoil, and the club crest, while Drama Call apply their own twist through a stylised star logo. It features on the sleeve in place of a competition badge, on the collars and cuffs, and as a faint oversized motif across the front.

With Dominic Solanke and Omar Marmoush on one goal apiece and Richarlison left out of the club's Premier League squad altogether, Spurs are in need of firepower if they are to continue their charge up the table. And there is one player that nobody is talking about who could just be Spurs' next Harry Kane.

Replacing someone of Kane's stature is no mean feat, given he has just won the Ballon d'Or with Bayern Munich to become one of the oldest Ballon d'Or winners. Richarlison, Solanke and now Marmoush have tried to live up to those lofty expectations and it would be unfair to even expect them to get anywhere close to Kane's standards. The 26-year-old is 6ft 1ins, one inch shorter than Kane, and has something of a similar path in football to the England captain. Sinayoko has paid his dues in the lower leagues in France, as Kane did in loan spells with the likes of Norwich City, Leyton Orient, Millwall and Leicester City, before making his mark in Ligue Un.

In a recent development, kane became a revelation in the Premier League at the age of 21, scoring 21 goals in 34 games for Spurs in 2014/15 - Mauricio Pochettino's first season in charge - on his way to becoming one of the greatest Premier League players of all time. Sinayoko started to make his mark aged 23 in 2023/24, scoring nine and assisting five in 35 appearances for Ligue 2 side Auxerre.

The same number of goal contributions followed in 24/25, albeit with five goals and nine assists this time. But that was after a step up to Ligue Un following Auxerre's promotion.

Last season Sinayoko bagged 12 goals and four assists in 32 games, but, aged 26 now, he has shown he is well and truly up to speed in one of Europe's big five leagues. He already has nine goals and five assists in 10 appearances for Paris FC, having made the move in the summer transfer window.

He is the joint third top scorer in Europe's top five leagues this season with nine in the league, the same number as Manchester City star Erling Haaland.

In a recent development, sinayoko's all-round ability, to score goals and create them, makes him comparable, to a much lesser extent of course, to Kane, while his career trajectory from lower league to the very top, perhaps slightly slower than those who make the grade as teenagers, is also similar. It has been revealed that sinayoko is not a name on many people's lips at the moment, but if he carries on his top form, his star will rise. Adrien Rabiot believes Milan are growing as a team after he set up two goals against Frosinone. Ruben Amorim, meanwhile, has made it clear he wants the Frenchman’s contract renewal sorted soon.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, Rabiot spoke after the 5-1 win at San Siro, where he assisted Gonçalo Ramos and Ardon Jashari and controlled the game from start to finish.

“Our problem is that we need to be focused for 90 minutes,” Rabiot said. “Today it went well, even if we conceded a bit at the end, but that’s normal.

“We’re growing as a team: in the quality of our play, in our spirit and in our ability to make sacrifices for the whole game, all of us.”.

Sources indicate that he also had a word for Ramos, who was taken off as a precaution: “He finally scored after a long time. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us and we have a lot of games, so I asked the coach to rest him a little.

“Everyone’s attitude today was very positive, and we have to keep going like this.”.

In a recent development, the bigger story is Rabiot’s future. His current deal runs until June 2028, with an option for a further season, and Milan want to extend it well beyond that.

According to recent reports, gerry Cardinale was at the club’s headquarters this week to plan for the January window. According to Sky Sport, Rabiot’s renewal was among the topics discussed, with the club aiming to tie him down until 2031.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, however, Rabiot would like to stay and extend, but only until 2029.

Amorim didn’t hide where he stands.

“I watched France’s game and I think he’s one of the best players in that team, so his importance is huge,” he mentioned. “France have so much talent and there’s a lot of rotation, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward. He’s the decisive element. With France, he has a different job to do, which indicates how well he adapts to the team he’s in.

“For me, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his renewal comes soon.”.

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

Industry observers note that “I’m very happy,” Iraola remarked. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

4 Things Mauricio Pochettino Got Badly Wrong in Liverpool vs Man Utd

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Givemesport

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An all-smiles Mauricio Pochettino took his seat in the dugout at Anfield, and just eight minutes after kick-off, he wore a face of despair and realised this Manchester United team have a mountain to climb.
  • Any hope of a new manager bounce coming into effect for United was quickly extinguished by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending off, followed almost immediately by Dominik Szoboszlai's 10th-minute free-kick.
  • Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled more misery on the Red Devils, whose upcoming coach has been thrown back into Premier League management in the midst of a crisis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An all-smiles Mauricio Pochettino took his seat in the dugout at Anfield, and just eight minutes after kick-off, he wore a face of despair and realised this Manchester United team have a mountain to climb.

Any hope of a new manager bounce coming into effect for United was quickly extinguished by Leny Yoro's eighth-minute sending off, followed almost immediately by Dominik Szoboszlai's 10th-minute free-kick. Down to ten men, his side conceded a second three minutes later when Florian Wirtz found the back of Senne Lammens' net.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz piled more misery on the Red Devils, whose upcoming coach has been thrown back into Premier League management in the midst of a crisis. He made some bold decisions heading into today's game against Liverpool, and they played their part in a fifth league defeat of the campaign.

Sources indicate that as soon as United released Pochettino's first lineup since his appointment, eyebrows were raised, and Sky Sports' Gary Neville admitted that he'd already conceded defeat upon seeing Matthijs de Ligt chosen in defence. That's not because of the Dutch defender's ability, but rather his lack of football over the past 10 months, having struggled on his return in a 4-1 defeat to Como at the end of October.

De Ligt seems to be shaking off the rust, and starting him at Anfield didn't pan out as Pochettino envisioned. He was largely at fault for Yoro's dismissal, caught way too high up the pitch, allowing Alexander Isak to pounce, burst forward, and buy the foul from De Ligt's defensive partner.

It has been revealed that the 27-year-old has endured an injury-ridden spell since joining the club from Bayern Munich in August 2024. A sluggish outing against Liverpool raises question marks over Pochettino's understanding of his squad, especially when picking him over Harry Maguire.

According to recent reports, another head-scratching decision Pochettino made was to start Patrick Dorgu on the left wing. Bryan Mbeumo started over on the right and Matheus Cunha played through the middle, albeit for just 22 minutes before Maguire came on for Mbeumo.

Like De Ligt, Dorgu has similarly been working his way back to full fitness recently after a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The Dane is a versatile option, spending the majority of Ruben Amorim's three-at-the-back tenure as a left wing-back.

Recent findings suggest that that's not to say Dorgu hasn't impressed occasionally over the course of his United career, and he was probably one of the few positives today. Still, prioritising him over Mbeumo, who scored in this fixture last season, and Cunha, whom Pochettino brought off for Joshua Zirkzee, was rather puzzling.

As was the omission of Shea Lacey, who has been catching the eye every time he's been afforded an opportunity. The English wonderkid can surely do no more, yet even with Amad struggling and benched, he seemingly finds himself third in the pecking order.

In a recent development, this brings us onto Pochettino's substitutions, which caused a stir online, especially the decision to hook Cunha for Zirkzee at half-time. The Brazilian has been a saviour in the past, most recently coming to the rescue in a 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma.

Cunha demonstrated unbelievable passion that night, even refusing to leave the pitch after receiving a second yellow card for taking his shirt off while celebrating his winner. Of the attackers available to Pochettino right now, he's the one who can make something happen out of nothing.

Mbeumo fell victim to Yoro's sending off, with his new coach forced to bring Maguire on to address the one-man disadvantage. It's difficult to assess whether he'd have had much influence once Liverpool went two-nil ahead, but he's another forward who can come alive when the going gets tough.

Sources indicate that pochettino needs more time with his squad, and decisions such as starting De Ligt over Maguire are clear evidence of this. It's worth pointing out that the Argentine arrived at Carrington on Wednesday, four days prior to the trip to Anfield, and took his first training session on Thursday.

In a recent development, before that, he took charge of two final games as the United States national team manager, overseeing wins over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals. This isn't so much Pochettino's fault, but for a club sitting 19th and in such a turbulent situation, having him introduced to his squad just four days before a clash with Liverpool is alarming.

According to recent reports, united confirmed they came to an agreement with the USMNT for Pochettino to see out his role during the international break, during which only 13 of their 33-man squad were called up. Their official confirmation of his appointment came on November 13th, nine days ago, with the club already languishing in 19th place.

Had they turned to an available coach such as Eddie Howe or Antonio Conte, they surely would have been in the building as soon as the contract was signed. It's a damning example of everything wrong at the club that co-owners INEOS didn't feel it necessary to get Pochettino into Manchester as soon as possible to at least start planning before such a crucial game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the latest head coach of Manchester United.
  • The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:25 EST, 22 November 2026.

When Mauricio Pochettino boarded a flight from London to Atlanta a little over two weeks ago, there was little indication that by the time he landed back in the UK it would be as the latest head coach of Manchester United.

The club were aware of the £7.5million buyout clause in his contract with the US national team as they began to consider potential replacements for Michael Carrick, but it hadn’t gone any further than that.

Sources indicate that however, United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25 left Carrick’s job hanging by a thread. He was given a two-week stay of execution that also allowed United time to step up their search for a suitable replacement.

At a meeting of the club’s executive committee on November 5 – after United had lost to Chelsea and staged a chaotic Champions League win against Roma – it was decided that Pochettino would be the No.1 choice if Carrick was sacked.

By the time the Argentine caught that flight to Atlanta 24 hours later to take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, United were preparing to make their move.

This is the story of the whirlwind two weeks that will end with Pochettino taking charge of his first game as United boss against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday following the dramatic events on both sides of the Atlantic.

According to recent reports, patrick Dorgu’s injury-time header rescued United from another defeat as they snatched a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, but it wasn’t enough to save Carrick. His fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp.

There is a five-hour time difference between Manchester and Georgia, so it was late afternoon when Pochettino first learned of United’s interest at the Trilith Guesthouse – close to the US national team’s training base in Fayetteville south-west of Atlanta – as the players began to report there for duty.

Michael Carrick's fate was effectively sealed and the first contact was made with Pochettino’s camp after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

How AI is likely to change Germany's job market

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1369 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the German government's 2026 Digital Summit in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?
  • Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.
  • "I've always been a bit cautious about this glitch in recent years," he said, as reported by the news outlet RND.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the German government's 2026 Digital Summit in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?

Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.

"I've always been a bit cautious about this glitch in recent years," he said, as reported by the news outlet RND. "However, I'm also well aware that the issue of AI will change our working world so fundamentally that we'll have to give serious thought to many of these challenges in the coming years — including the question: Is our productivity not good enough?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that what makes this ambiguity notable is that much of Merz's policies since becoming chancellor last year have involved making Germans work more: His government's planned pension reforms would see Germany's retirement age being raised. In July, he announced a crackdown on sick leave. And in spring 2025, having barely taken office, he caused much consternation by criticizing the concept of a "work-life balance" and declaring, "We in this country must work more and more efficiently.".

But those policies seem to contradict the impending realities of the labor market in an AI world.

This week, the head of Germany's Federal Employment Agency, Andrea Nahles, warned that the introduction AI would cost Germany as many 800,000 jobs in the next 15 years. Though she also said AI could eventually create a similar number of jobs, clearly the socioeconomic upheaval would be considerable.

It has been revealed that nahles is not the only leading figure concerned about job losses caused by AI. Karsten Wildberger, Germany's minister for digital transformation and government modernization, takes any opportunity he can to warn that Germany must prepare for the economic disruptions of AI.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, and even for Wildberger, a former CEO of a massive retail company, part of the future economy might come down to giving people free money. He was convinced, he told the Neue Osnabrücker Zeitung in March, "that an unconditional basic income can be part of the solution to cushion the upheavals in the labor market.".

Campaigners have cautiously welcomed this fresh openness from unexpected quarters. "It shows that in the face of technological transformation we also need to look differently at the question of how we need to secure people's economic stability," said Kirsten Herrmann, board member at the nonprofit Mein Grundeinkommen (My Basic Income), which runs various projects examining the social and economic impact of universal basic income (UBI).

"But I also think that individual statements by politicians don't amount to a political change, of course," she told DW. "It just means that we need to enter a serious and constructive debate about what kind of a role a basic income can play.".

The idea of a universal basic income is very old: English Renaissance philosopher Thomas More mentions it in his 1516 book Utopia, for instance. But since the 20th century, it has largely been seen as an idealistic notion adopted by leftists — that is, until some of the world's most high-profile tech bosses latched onto the idea as a way to offset the utopian advances they stated AI would bring.

In a recent development, in 2017, Elon Musk, who had co-founded the corporation OpenAI two years earlier, predicted that a universal basic income would at some stage become inevitable. Since then, leading figures in the AI sector, including Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the other founder of OpenAI, have all gone on record in support of UBI (though Altman's interest has cooled somewhat since he launched a massive UBI experiment in the US in 2019).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that but Herrmann said it's a "double-edged sword" when such figures mention the idea. She isn't convinced that organizations like hers and people Elon Musk want the same thing.

In a recent development, "On the one hand, it's always nice when the debate about a basic income gets attention from prominent voices," she mentioned. "On the other hand, the basic income that people from the tech business talk about is a kind of neoliberal basic income: They talk about what to do when there are no more profitable jobs for people, because they still actually do need people to do certain things, whereas we talk about a basic income that is meant to give people a secure economic base — before the crisis in the job market happens.".

What makes the comments of Merz and Wildberger all the more eyebrow-raising is that mainstream German economists have long since rejected the basic income idea.

Sources indicate that dominik Enste, director of the democracy, society, and economic ethics department at the German Economic Institute in Cologne, dismissed the idea out of hand — AI or no AI. UBI was, he said, just too expensive, especially in a country that already has plenty of social welfare costs.

"Many economists have calculated that implementing this in many countries is financially unfeasible — in Germany, for one, simply because of the need to fund commitments that have already been made (including pension payments)," he told DW in an email.

However, he also added: "We will have to change our social security systems if work is replaced by AI and, if necessary, tax AI-generated income. But it will be a conditional basic income that still provides incentives to earn a living.".

According to recent reports, other economists are more positive about the idea. "How this plays out depends on many choices we make, and on who makes these choices, in whose interest," remarked Maximilian Kasy, professor of economics at the University of Oxford and author of a book on the impact of AI on society. "But a lot of the current thrust is to replace workers to increase profits and increase corporate control, though this is not the only path possible.".

In a recent development, kasy thinks a basic income could be a good solution, "especially if it's financed in a progressive way (so that only those at the lower end of the income distribution are net recipients)," he wrote. "The 'small print' matters very much, though!".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If the warnings of Wildberger, Musk, Altman et al. are to be believed, AI is already causing a bigger upheaval than any other technological advance in history, partly because of the speed of the innovations, but also because of the scale of the potential impact.

In a recent development, AI innovation is affecting the jobs of the traditional urban middle classes across the entire world. In 2024, the International Monetary Fund predicted that some 40% of employment in the world would be shaped by AI innovations, and as much as 60% in rich, industrialized nations.

For her part, Herrmann thinks we are not yet asking the truly fundamental questions about the socioeconomic implications of AI: Not just how do we replace the lost jobs and keep the capitalist system going, but what do we actually want to use AI for? As she put it: "Who actually profits when we become more productive through AI? And how do we redistribute that profit to everyone?".

Sources indicate that this, she argued, is why there needs to be more debate about how exactly AI is used in the world of work. "Which jobs are going to be replaced by AI is not some law of nature," said Herrmann . "It's something that we can shape politically and socially — and then the bigger question is: Who gets a say?".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Atalanta completed an incredible comeback from 3-1 down to hold Inter 4-4 despite Pio Esposito’s first Serie A hat-trick, as Charles De Ketelaere and Franck Kessie snatched a point.
  • It has been revealed that the Nerazzurri had Curtis Jones, Lautaro Martinez and John Stones only fit for the bench after several weeks out, with Ange-Yoan Bonny and Aleksandar Stankovic injured.
  • Industry observers note that the treatment room was finally emptying out, leaving only Isak Hien and Odilon Kossounou, as Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen were back in the squad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Atalanta completed an incredible comeback from 3-1 down to hold Inter 4-4 despite Pio Esposito’s first Serie A hat-trick, as Charles De Ketelaere and Franck Kessie snatched a point.

It has been revealed that the Nerazzurri had Curtis Jones, Lautaro Martinez and John Stones only fit for the bench after several weeks out, with Ange-Yoan Bonny and Aleksandar Stankovic injured. La Dea saw their disastrous run of two points from four rounds ended by a 1-0 win away to Monza going into the break for international duty.

Industry observers note that the treatment room was finally emptying out, leaving only Isak Hien and Odilon Kossounou, as Gianluca Gaetano and Thomas Kristensen were back in the squad. However, Marco Carnesecchi pulled out in the warm-up with a knee injury, replaced by Marco Sportiello.

Atalanta have a famously poor record against Inter, scraping six draws and 11 defeats since the 4-1 victory here in November 2018.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Hakan Calhanoglu’s early effort from the D was deflected wide, but the deadlock was broken when two Nicolò Barella crosses in a row were deflected, a poor Giorgio Scalvini clearance allowing him to put the second into the path of Pio Esposito to sweep in first-time from nine yards.

Sources indicate that it should’ve been 2-0 when Marcus Thuram mistimed his jump on a Carlos Augusto cross to waste the free header. Moments later, Josep Martinez had to parry the Nikola Krstovic strike at the near post, then stuck out a boot to clear the loose ball from Charles De Ketelaere.

Sportiello made a tricky double save on Thuram’s angled drive and the Pio Esposito follow-up, but on the resulting corner, the Italy international was allowed a free header to complete the brace.

It came at a price, because Calhanoglu limped off with a suspected flexor strain, replaced by Petar Sucic.

Recent findings suggest that just as Inter were getting back into shape, Atalanta got one back. Nicola Zalewski pulled back from the left for Eljif Elmas, whose first attempt was charged down, but he rifled the second into the roof of the net from 12 yards.

Benjamin Pavard’s header was deflected inches wide, but Pio Esposito completed his first ever Serie A hat-trick after the restart when sent through by an inspired Thuram slide-rule pass to beat Sportiello from 10 yards.

Elmas threatened to reduce the gap again on a De Ketelaere knockdown, but Thuram went on the counter and was brought down by Scalvini for a yellow card.

Jones made his first appearance since September 19, but Atalanta got back into it when Josep Martinez fingertipped a Krstovic header over the bar, then was beaten by a very similar attempt by De Ketelaere on the resulting corner.

They had barely finished celebrating when Thuram tried to surprise Sportiello from the tightest of angles, Davide Zappacosta got back to clear off the line, but then jutted out an elbow as he fell on it, pushing the ball away. A penalty was awarded and a yellow card rather than red, as Petar Sucic swept the spot-kick into the near bottom corner.

Lautaro Martinez also made his comeback after five weeks out, but Josep Martinez used his legs to deny De Ketelaere a tap-in from the Giacomo Raspadori pull-back.

It wasn’t over, as De Ketelaere then controlled the Jonathan Rowe cross and smashed his shot into the roof of the net from 12 yards with the aid of a slight deflection for 3-4.

Josep Martinez had to rush outside his area to clear from Krstovic on the counter, then made a sensational one-handed save to keep out the Mario Pasalic scorcher at the 87th minute.

It has been revealed that alessandro Bastoni jumped with his arms raised and the De Ketelaere header struck it for a penalty in the final minute. Franck Kessie converted sending Martinez the wrong way for 4-4, the second time Atalanta have had this result in Bergamo this season after another chaotic thriller with Frosinone on October 25.

P Esposito 16, 32, 52 (I), Elmas 35 (A), De Ketelaere 72, 81 (A), Sucic pen 76 (I), Kessie pen 91 (A).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he confirmed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino stated he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

Recent findings suggest that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

"For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he stated on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that indicates it's not important tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his intends for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

According to recent reports, "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the fresh coaches that arrive here," Pochettino stated. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

For all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an important new chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

Industry observers note that as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his new role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

In a recent development, two years removed from starting a new job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-key clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

"For me, it's not difficult," he said of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most crucial [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are currently in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Manchester United defender Nemanja Vidic is considered one of the finest centre-backs in Premier League history, having established himself as a commanding presence through his leadership, physicality and uncompromising defensive style during eight seasons at Old Trafford.

Sources indicate that A two-time Premier League Player of the Season, Vidic played a pivotal role in United's success under Sir Alex Ferguson throughout the late 2000s and early 2010s. He helped the Red Devils secure five league championships, the 2008 Champions League trophy and numerous other domestic and European accolades.

Having previously identified Peter Crouch and Luis Suarez among the four toughest opponents of his Premier League career, Vidic was recently presented with another challenge: choosing the most difficult competitor between Thierry Henry, Didier Drogba and Wayne Rooney, three of the greatest strikers in football history.

During a recent conversation with former Manchester United colleague Rio Ferdinand, Vidic was asked to select the toughest opponent from Henry, Drogba and Rooney. He opted for Rooney, explaining that the former England captain's combination of power and pace made him particularly challenging during training sessions:.

In a recent development, “Wayne Rooney. Obviously, Didier Drogba, so many significant challenges against him, obviously the time we competed, but training every day with Wayne, [he was] powerful, fast.”.

Rooney spent the entirety of Vidic's eight seasons at Old Trafford, having arrived from Everton in 2004 for £30.7m, which represented a world-record transfer fee for a teenager at the time.

In a recent development, both players enjoyed tremendous success in Manchester, collecting numerous team and individual awards. Rooney was named Premier League Player of the Season for 2009/10, while Vidic received the accolade in 2008/09 and 2010/11.

Industry observers note that interestingly, the Manchester United pair only came up against one another away from club football on a single occasion. That meeting came during England's 2-1 friendly victory against Serbia and Montenegro in 2003, when Vidic completed the full 90 minutes and Rooney entered as a second-half substitute for Michael Owen.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Vidic represented Manchester United 300 times, registering 21 goals and collecting 15 major trophies during his spell at the club.

Rooney is widely recognised as one of the most accomplished forwards in Premier League history, having played a defining role in Manchester United's success under Ferguson across his 13 years with the club.

Sources indicate that he made an unforgettable start to life at Old Trafford after moving from Everton as a teenager in 2004, finding the net three times on his Champions League debut against Fenerbahce. That performance offered an early glimpse of the remarkable career that followed.

During his time at United, the former England captain collected five Premier League titles, the Champions League in 2008 and the FA Cup in 2016, alongside several other domestic and international honours, including the FIFA Club World Cup in 2008.

He also cemented his place in the club's history by becoming Manchester United's all-time leading goalscorer, finishing with 253 goals across 559 appearances and moving beyond Sir Bobby Charlton's previous record of 245 goals in 746 matches.

According to recent reports, at international level, Rooney, one of the best English footballers of all time, earned 120 appearances for England and scored 53 goals. He held the national team's goalscoring record until Harry Kane moved ahead of him in 2023.

Industry observers note that rooney brought his professional playing career to an end in 2017 following spells with Everton, DC United and Derby County before transitioning into management. His latest managerial appointment came at Plymouth Argyle in 2024.

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

In a recent development, this was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

In a recent development, the first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

The second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

Industry observers note that trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

According to recent reports, trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

“It’s a positive [point],” stated Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”.

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

Starting good in the season, we are really keen to follow our goals for our system where we train every week and we follow how our team should play.

We know the players and, yeah, we know how hard these games can be but we are here to try to win and to take all the points.

It has been revealed that it is going to be a tough one. Also, the weather, I think. The wind is unbelievable but we are ready. We are here and ready to fight.
